verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds; nothing is missing and no content differs. 1. NOTHING IS MISSING. The rendered PDF page 1139 (printed folio 1109) prints the bold heading 'D.19.4.2 Method invocation'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:45813 contains '## D.19.4.2 Method invocation', preceded at :45812 by the correct anchor ''. Clause number, title text, and cross-reference anchor are all present and verbatim correct. The kind label 'missing-heading' is a misnomer for what is at most a differing '#' count; the claim's own markdown_says field quotes the heading it calls missing. 2. THE CLAIM'S TYPOGRAPHIC PREMISE IS SELF-DEFEATING. I rendered both pages. Page 1138 prints 'D.19.4 Methods' and 'D.19.4.1 General' in the SAME bold face and size; page 1139 prints 'D.19.4.2 Method invocation' in that same face and size. ISO uses one uniform heading style for Annex D subclauses at all of these depths, so the PDF supplies NO typographic rank signal at all here - depth is conveyed solely by the dotted clause number. Applied consistently, the claim's criterion ('the PDF prints them at the same rank, so they must share a markdown level') would equally demand that the PARENT D.19.4 Methods sit at the same level as D.19.4.1 - i.e. it would vindicate '##' and condemn '###'. The claim silently picks D.19.4.1 as normative without justification. 3. HEADING DEPTH IS NOT A CLAUSE HIERARCHY ANYWHERE IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION, SO NO TREE IS BEING DAMAGED. The file carries 1233 page-break markers emitted as LEVEL-2 headings ('## Page NNNN'), plus running headers emitted as LEVEL-1 ('# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'). One such pair sits nine lines above the disputed heading (:45804 '## Page 1139', :45806 '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)'). Under any markdown outline reading, that level-2 page marker - and the level-1 running header above it - already close '## D.19.4 Methods' before D.19.4.2 is ever reached. So 'D.19.4.2 is not nested under D.19.4' is true regardless of whether it is written '##' or '###', and is true of essentially every clause in the document that spans a page break. This is whole-file page-break furniture, exactly the category the verification rules say to reject, not a page-1139 defect. 4. THE LEVEL ASSIGNMENT TRACKS NOTHING DOCUMENT-WIDE, SO IT CARRIES NO INFORMATION TO LOSE. Sampling D.x clause headings: four-component numbers appear at '####' (D.9.2.1, D.20.3.2, D.14.2.2), at '###' (D.19.4.1, D.19.3.4), and at '##' (D.19.4.2, D.19.4.3, D.19.5.2, D.19.9.3); three-component numbers appear at '####' (D.2.2), '###' (D.19.2) and '##' (D.19.3, D.19.5.4); five-component numbers appear at '###' (D.6.5.6.2) and '##' (D.19.5.4.2). The '#' count is not a function of clause depth anywhere in the file. Meaning in this spec is carried by the dotted clause number and the body text - both byte-correct here - and cross-referencing is carried by the anchor id, which is also correct. No text is lost, reflowed, altered, or reordered on page 1139. The sole difference is one markdown formatting character count in a document whose heading levels are already non-hierarchical by construction, and it changes no meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. The heading 'D.19.4.2 Method invocation' is present in the markdown verbatim with a correct anchor; nothing is missing, so 'missing-heading' misdescribes it. The PDF prints D.19.4, D.19.4.1 and D.19.4.2 in one identical bold style, giving no typographic rank signal to reproduce - so the claim's premise would equally condemn the sibling it treats as correct. Separately, the transcription's '#' depth is not a clause hierarchy at all: 1233 page breaks are emitted as level-2 '## Page NNNN' headings (one nine lines above this heading) and running headers as level-1, and D.x clause numbers of identical depth appear at '##', '###' and '####' throughout the annex. If anything is worth tracking, it is a document-wide cosmetic normalization of transcription heading levels - not a page-1139 structural finding, and not something that affects the meaning, citability, or cross-referenceability of D.19.4.2.
